<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Bind measurements at a common date, derive BMI, mean arterial pressure and a
ratio, and check the inputs needed for eGFR and duplicate handling.
</div>

**You need:** the packages, downloaded helpers and two loaded resources in
[Before you start](book-00-start.html#before-you-start), plus the recipe basics
from [chapter 6](book-06-events.html). Start a fresh R session in `book-work`.
Run the sections in order: each uses objects defined immediately above it.

These are **public synthetic Synthea27Nj patients**, from the pinned Eunomia
archive used by the numeric validation loader. There are 28 fictional people,
not 27. GiBleed is the other practice resource and has no populated numeric
measurement values. All results below were executed with dsOMOP 2.10.5.

Concept selections refer to the searches and saved definitions in
[chapter 4](book-04-vocabulary.html), including the separate questionnaire
catalogue. Additional body-measurement concepts are found on screen in the
[formula walkthrough](book-15-formulas.html#find-the-inputs-before-calculating).

## Find the inputs before calculating

Use the same Synthea resource as the lab chapter. A formula does not make inputs
comparable: check the measurement meaning, units and date before combining them.


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
source("tools/book/case-helpers.R")
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
```

Search weight and height separately. The search rows carry standard status,
concept class and validity dates. Select an exact name, not the first search hit.


``` r
weight_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body weight", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
height_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body height", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(rbind(weight_hits, height_hits)[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")])
```



|concept_name |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|:------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|Body weight  |S                |LOINC         |
|Body height  |S                |LOINC         |

``` r
weight_id <- weight_hits$concept_id[trimws(weight_hits$concept_name) == "Body weight"]
height_id <- height_hits$concept_id[trimws(height_hits$concept_name) == "Body height"]
body_sets <- list(weight = omop_concept_set(weight_id), height = omop_concept_set(height_id))
```


``` r
weight_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = weight_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
height_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = height_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(weight_units)
```



|   n|concept_name |value |
|---:|:------------|:-----|
| 510|kilogram     |9529  |

``` r
knitr::kable(height_units)
```



|   n|concept_name |value |
|---:|:------------|:-----|
| 495|centimeter   |8582  |

The unit IDs used below were returned by those protected inventories. In the
pinned source they mean kilogram and centimetre, as also inspected in chapter 4.

## Bind weight and height on the same day

Index on first weight. The exact-day tolerance selects both inputs at that date.
An absent height stays missing; choosing a distant height silently would change
the formula's meaning. Synthea includes children, so do not apply adult BMI bands.


``` r
weight_event <- omop_event("measurement", body_sets$weight)
weight <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$weight, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = 9529L)
height <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$height, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = 8582L)
```

## Declare BMI with the closed expression grammar

The small `book_col`, `book_lit`, `book_op` and `book_expr` helpers construct
plain data lists; their source is in the downloadable helpers. For example:


``` r
book_expr(book_op("/", book_col("weight"), book_col("height")))
```

```
#> $version
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $assign
#> $assign[[1]]
#> $assign[[1]]$name
#> [1] "result"
#> 
#> $assign[[1]]$expr
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$op
#> [1] "/"
#> 
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$args
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$args[[1]]
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$args[[1]]$col
#> [1] "weight"
#> 
#> 
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$args[[2]]
#> $assign[[1]]$expr$args[[2]]$col
#> [1] "height"
```

No arbitrary R or SQL runs on the server. BMI is kg divided by metres squared.
The expression below converts cm squared to metres squared with a factor of 10,000.


``` r
bmi <- omop_number_derive(list(weight = weight, height = height),
  book_expr(book_op("/", book_op("*", book_col("weight"), book_lit(10000)),
    book_op("*", book_col("height"), book_col("height")))), unit = "coordinate:bmi_kg_m2")
body <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(weight = weight, height = height, bmi = bmi))
print(recipe_execute(body, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_body"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>         baseline 
#> "D_formula_body"
```

``` r
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_body$bmi", datasources = conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        | 11.53374|
|site |10%       | 13.62216|
|site |25%       | 15.88957|
|site |50%       | 23.86380|
|site |75%       | 27.93787|
|site |90%       | 30.20849|
|site |95%       | 30.36386|
|site |Mean      | 22.11315|

Inputs default to their canonical numeric stage. Presentation rounding does not
silently round a formula input. Division by zero and missing inputs yield missing
values. A coordinate name documents the derived result; it does not validate a
clinical formula or create a unit conversion automatically.

**Exercise 1.** Round BMI to one decimal for presentation while keeping the
unrounded formula available.

<details><summary>Solution 1</summary>


``` r
body_rounded <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(bmi = bmi, rounded = omop_number(bmi,
    omop_number_spec(rounding = omop_number_round("decimals", 1)))))
print(recipe_execute(body_rounded, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_rounded"), conns = conns))
```

```

#> "D_formula_rounded"
```

## Mean arterial pressure and a ratio

Find systolic and diastolic pressure, inspect their recorded units, then bind both
to the same systolic measurement date. The familiar approximate MAP formula is
(SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3; it is a derived estimate, not a separately measured pressure.


``` r
sbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Systolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
dbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Diastolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(rbind(sbp_hits, dbp_hits)[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")])
```



|concept_name                          |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|:-------------------------------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|Systolic blood pressure               |S                |LOINC         |
|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|Diastolic blood pressure              |S                |LOINC         |

``` r
sbp_id <- sbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(sbp_hits$concept_name) == "Systolic blood pressure"]
dbp_id <- dbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(dbp_hits$concept_name) == "Diastolic blood pressure"]
knitr::kable(ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = sbp_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
```



|   n|concept_name              |value |
|---:|:-------------------------|:-----|
| 725|millimeter mercury column |8876  |


``` r
sbp_event <- omop_event("measurement", omop_concept_set(sbp_id))
sbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", sbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = 8876L)
dbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", dbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = 8876L)
map <- omop_number_derive(list(sbp = sbp, dbp = dbp),
  book_expr(book_op("/", book_op("+", book_col("sbp"),
    book_op("*", book_lit(2), book_col("dbp"))), book_lit(3))), unit = "unit:8876")
ratio <- omop_number_derive(list(sbp = sbp, dbp = dbp),
  book_expr(book_op("/", book_col("sbp"), book_col("dbp"))), unit = "1")
pressure <- omop_study(sbp_event, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(map = map, ratio = ratio))
print(recipe_execute(pressure, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_pressure"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>             baseline 
#> "D_formula_pressure"
```


## eGFR: validate the prerequisites before deriving

The race-free adult CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation needs serum creatinine,
age and sex. Its public formula is
142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^−1.2 × 0.9938^age,
with κ = 0.7 and α = −0.241 for female, κ = 0.9 and α = −0.302
for male, and a further factor 1.012 for female. Scr is in mg/dL.
See the [National Kidney Foundation equation](https://www.kidney.org/professionals/ckd-epi-creatinine-equation-2021).

Do not substitute a different specimen because the correct source is sparse.
This check distinguishes vocabulary availability from observed use:


``` r
creatinine_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Creatinine", domain = "Measurement",
  vocabulary = "LOINC", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(creatinine_hits[c("concept_name", "standard_concept")])
```



|concept_name                                  |standard_concept |
|:---------------------------------------------|:----------------|
|Microalbumin/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in Urine |S                |
|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma   |S                |
|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Blood             |S                |

``` r
serum_id <- creatinine_hits$concept_id[trimws(creatinine_hits$concept_name) ==
  "Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma"]
serum_set <- omop_concept_set(serum_id)
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.locate(serum_id, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
```

The pinned subset's populated creatinine concept is **Blood**, while the formula
requests Serum or Plasma. This lesson therefore does not report patient eGFR.
The A-29 build used here has no named CKD-EPI helper: `omop_number_derive` accepts
closed arithmetic, while powers can be composed from log, affine and exp stages.
A production definition still needs validated specimen equivalence, aligned age
and sex, adult eligibility and formula validation. A published formula alone is
not permission to change the source semantics.

**Exercise 3.** Why would using the first creatinine search hit be unsafe? Save
the intended serum definition instead.

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
formula_concepts <- list(body = body_sets, systolic = omop_concept_set(sbp_id),
  diastolic = omop_concept_set(dbp_id), serum_creatinine = serum_set)
formula_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(formula_concepts, formula_file)
identical(readRDS(formula_file), formula_concepts)
```

```
#> [1] TRUE
```

Name matching is a discovery aid. The intended specimen, unit and source use
must all agree before formula execution.

</details>

## Collapse repeated episodes deliberately

A person may have several eligible measurement episodes. Requesting person grain
requires an explicit collapse rule: first_episode, last_episode or any. This
collapses repeated population episodes, not duplicate source measurements.


``` r
episodes <- omop_population("weights", index = omop_index(weight_event, select = "all"))
collapsed <- omop_recipe(populations = list(episodes), variables = list(weight = weight),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "weights", format = "wide", grain = "person",
    collapse = "first_episode"))
cat(grep("collapse|grain", recipe_explain(collapsed)$text, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

```
#> Output 'people' [wide] rows 'weights', grain person (collapse first_episode)
#>   - output 'people': one row per person from an episode population, collapse = "first_episode"
```

``` r
print(recipe_execute(collapsed, out = c(people = "D_collapsed_weights"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>                people 
#> "D_collapsed_weights"
```

``` r
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_collapsed_weights$weight", datasources = conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        |  2.71000|
|site |10%       |  3.73000|
|site |25%       | 11.05000|
|site |50%       | 70.90000|
|site |75%       | 75.72500|
|site |90%       | 80.94000|
|site |95%       | 84.83500|
|site |Mean      | 50.44643|

A same-day tolerance still does not average duplicate readings automatically.
Closest-value selection uses deterministic ordering; a mean weights eligible
rows. Document whether the problem is repeated episodes or duplicated source
records before choosing a collapse or reducer. The events chapter compares
record counts with distinct-day counts.

**Exercise 4.** Choose the last eligible episode instead. Predict the selection
before comparing its summary with the first-episode output.

<details><summary>Solution 4</summary>


``` r
last_episode <- collapsed
last_episode$outputs$people$collapse <- "last_episode"
print(recipe_execute(last_episode, out = c(people = "D_last_weights"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>           people 
#> "D_last_weights"
```

measurement average, and it need not equal an average over all episodes.

## Recap

Align meanings, units and dates before arithmetic. Native expressions preserve
private inputs and declared coordinates. BMI, MAP and ratios use the closed
grammar; missing prerequisites are a reason to stop a formula study. Collapse
repeated episodes explicitly instead of letting duplicate rows change an analysis.
